mechanism_narrative: PDGFRA-IL6ST forced-proximity novokine with flexible GS4 linker (~20 Å) enables bidirectional transphosphorylation between an RTK (PDGFRA) and a cytokine receptor (IL6ST/gp130). PDGFRA's kinase domain phosphorylates IL6ST's intracellular tyrosines, creating STAT3 docking sites and amplifying JAK-STAT signaling. Reciprocally, JAK1/2 pre-associated with IL6ST phosphorylate PDGFRA tyrosines, enhancing GRB2-SHC1-SOS-RAS-MAPK and PI3K-AKT recruitment via GAB1/PIK3R1. PLCG1/2 are sterically excluded by the tight ~20 Å linker geometry and the 92 aa ECD asymmetry (505 vs 597 aa), which prevents productive PLCγ docking. The biased output is synergistic MAPK↑ + PI3K/AKT↑ + STAT3↑ signaling in FAPs (the primary co-expressing cell type in aged muscle), promoting muscle structural gene expression (ACTA2, MYL9, MYH11, MYOM2, TAGLN) and suppressing aged inflammatory/IEG programs (EGR1, FOS, JUN, IL32, TXNIP).
